subject: Unexpected November usage spike — backfill ingestion and credit request
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan@streamlytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@streamlytics.com, finance@streamlytics.com
Date: 2026-11-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: High November invoice — looks like a backfill

Hi Tessa,

We just received our November bill and noticed a ~1.2M token surge on Nov 25–26 that we didn't expect. Our ops team traced activity to a backfill job that replayed historical records into our ingestion pipeline; we believe many of those events were duplicates of production traffic. Attached is a small snapshot (usage_snapshot_20261127.csv) showing token counts by route.

Can you help clarify how Redwood attributes tokens for replays/backfills? We need to understand whether this is billable or if we can get a credit — this jump would push us over our committed tier.

Thanks — appreciate a quick look, we're on a tight billing cadence.

— Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform
Streamlytics

(Attachment: usage_snapshot_20261127.csv)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@streamlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High November invoice — looks like a backfill

Ethan — thanks for the heads-up and for the snapshot. I opened an internal investigation and temporarily flagged your Nov invoice for review so it doesn't auto-charge while we validate.

Quick context: by default, our metering counts tokens for every request that reaches the inference runtime, including replayed events, unless a customer provides an explicit ingest exclusion tag or we apply a manual adjustment. We will:

- Pull the audit logs for the ingestion window you highlighted
- Check request IDs for duplication and replay markers
- Estimate billable token delta and propose an adjustment if replayed traffic is confirmed

Ben — can you pull the request-level logs for 2026-11-24 through 11-26 (all regions) and look for duplicate request_ids or the replay flag? Monica, I'm looping you in for account coordination and to confirm whether Streamlytics has a committed tier that would be impacted.

Ethan — I expect an update within 24 hours. If we confirm replayed duplicates, we'll propose a credit and route the adjustment through your account.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 9:12 AM Ethan Cole <ethan@streamlytics.com> wrote:
> Hi Tessa,
>
> We just received our November bill and noticed a ~1.2M token surge...

(Attachment: usage_snapshot_20261127.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High November invoice — looks like a backfill (investigation findings)

Tessa / team — I've pulled the raw request logs and replay audit for the Streamlytics tenant. Summary:

- Backfill job started 2026-11-25T02:03:12Z and finished 2026-11-25T09:18:55Z (ingest pipeline ID: bf-20261125-49).
- During the window, ~1,210,442 additional inference requests reached the runtime.
- Of those, ~980,371 have request_ids that match requests we've already billed for in the preceding 30 days (same request_id pattern, identical payload hashes).
- The replay carries a replay_marker header set by Streamlytics' ingestion service (replay=true) but that header did not get mapped to our ingest exclusion tag — looks like the Streamlytics connector version did not transmit the mapping field.

Recommendation: propose a one-time credit for the duplicate portion (980,371 tokens billed). I've estimated the token-to-dollar at your current SKU rates; proposed credit amount = $9,235.30. I attached the filtered audit logs with request_id matches (audit_logs_replay_20261125.zip) for traceability.

Soojin — can you confirm whether the credit can be applied retroactively and what the billing ledger impact will be (reversal vs credit note)? Monica, once we confirm, I'll stage the credit and send an adjusted invoice.

Ben
Senior Billing Engineer
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: audit_logs_replay_20261125.zip)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan@streamlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T16:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High November invoice — looks like a backfill

Ethan — thanks for your patience. We completed our review and confirmed that ~980k of the additional requests were replayed duplicates and not new production traffic.

Action we've taken:
- Applied a one-time credit of $9,235.30 to the November invoice; the credit will appear as an adjusted invoice (attached: adjusted_invoice_20261128.pdf).
- Placed a note in your account indicating the connector mapping gap; Monica will follow up with recommended connector configuration to ensure replay=true maps to ingest_exclude for future jobs.
- Opened internal billing ticket BILL-3421 to prevent similar misses and to add an automated replay-header detection rule in the ingest pipeline.

Next steps for Streamlytics:
- Please confirm receipt of the adjusted invoice and that the credit amount aligns with your internal calculation.
- If you want us to automatically exclude future replay traffic, please deploy the connector patch (we can share a diff) or provide a mapping table and we'll apply a tenant-level rule.

Monica will reach out to schedule a 15-minute sync tomorrow to confirm closing items and to walk through the connector change.

Thanks again — sorry for the noise. Let me know if you'd like the raw matched-request report sent over (Ben attached it to the internal thread).

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: adjusted_invoice_20261128.pdf)
